summary: Redwood AE/SE demo focused on structured output (JSON mode), schema enforcement, and function/tool-calling. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a product feature that emits structured order-insights and fulfillment actions. Key concerns: deterministic JSON outputs, guardrails against hallucination, audit logs / SOC 2, and integration with their toolchain. Agreed next steps: send pricing + security docs, schedule pilot & benchmark, provide example schemas and Prompt patterns.
topics: Console demo: schema validation, examples, evals
Security: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok, hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we have Carlos and Priya with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alex: good, thanks. excited to see the structured output stuff - we got a list of questions.
[00:12] Maya: great, high level we'll show how JSON mode works, how function calling integrates, and then quick Console walkthrough for schemas and guardrails. Carlos will demo a live example with your sample prompt.
[00:24] Jordan: sounds good. our priority is that the output is deterministic JSON we can parse into downstream systems - and we need to avoid false fields being emitted.
[00:33] Carlos: yes, totally. in Redwood we have two patterns, one is the structured-output mode where you pass a schema and the model is guided to emit only matching fields, and the other is function/tool calling where the model returns a structured call payload that your runtime executes. We'll show both.
[00:47] Samira: quick question, are these only for hosted or can we run same patterns on dedicated/dedicated private?
[00:54] Maya: same APIs and Console features across hosted, Dedicated, and Private - you can pin versions and rollout policies.
[01:02] Ethan: security: do you keep logs? how's PII handled - KMS, retention?
[01:08] Priya: yes, we have audit logs, and encryption at rest with KMS/HSM options for Private. We also have retention controls you can set. We'll paste the SOC 2 and security pack after.
[01:17] Carlos: ok, jumping into the dev flow. (screen share) here's an example schema for an order-insights response - fields: order_id, risk_score, recommended_action, confidence, metadata. Watch how the model is constrained.
[01:32] [01:33] Carlos: prompt sent... oops small typo in the sample prompt - uh sorry.
[01:37] Jordan: no problem.
[01:39] [02:00] Carlos: returned JSON: {"order_id": "12345", "risk_score": 0.82, "recommended_action": "hold_for_review", "confidence": 0.87, "metadata": {"source": "payments"}} - you'll notice we also support schema coercion and type validation so numbers stay numbers, enums are validated.
[02:20] Alex: hmm in our experience models sometimes return strings like "0.82" for floats, how strict is the coercion?
[02:26] Carlos: we run a validation pass and can either coerce or fail the response based on your policy. The Console has toggles: strict mode (fail on mismatch) or permissive (attempt coercion and add warnings).
[02:39] Samira: and how do guardrails work when the model hallucinates an action, like inventing a new field?
[02:45] Carlos: we have three layers: 1) schema enforcement at generation-time using sampling constraints, 2) post-generation validator that strips/flags unexpected fields, and 3) function-calling execution policy that refuses to run unknown actions unless whitelisted. We'll demo a function-call next.
[03:02] Maya: also to note, you can add allowed enums and regex patterns in the schema to pin formats - helpful for order ids, skus, etc.
[03:11] [03:30] Carlos: ok live function-call demo - we define a tool called "fulfillment_action" with input schema: {action: enum[ship,cancel,hold], order_id: string, reason: optional string}. Send prompt instructing model to pick an action.
[03:45] [04:05] Carlos: model returned a function call payload: {"name": "fulfillment_action", "args": {"action": "ship", "order_id": "12345"}} - note Console shows the parsed call and you can preview execution.
[04:20] Jordan: if the model suggests something outside enum (like "expedite"), what happens?
[04:26] Carlos: if not whitelisted, execution is blocked; you can configure a fallback mapping (expedite -> ship + expedite flag) or reject. We recommend explicit mappings for safety-critical flows.
[04:37] Alex: great. what's the latency hit when you enable strict validation and schema enforcement?
[04:44] Priya: small, typically 10-30ms extra per request for validation; the bigger latency driver is model size and batching. Our SDK supports streaming structured chunks to keep latency low.
[04:55] Maya: also Optimize will recommend batching and quantization per-route to meet cost targets while hitting latency SLOs.
[05:03] [05:30] Samira: can you show the Console where we set schemas and view Eval results?
[05:35] Carlos: sure. (screen) Console -> Routes -> Create Route -> Output Schema. Here we import a JSON Schema or build visually. You can attach a suite of eval prompts and expected outputs; Console will run regressions on deploy.
[05:52] Carlos: here's a past regression: after a model bump the recommended_action changed distribution, Console flagged it and we rolled back.
[06:01] Alex: ok that is useful. On the pilot we want to run a 1-week benchmark - realistic traffic is spikey. What metrics should we collect?
[06:09] Carlos: collect p95 latency, token cost, error rate (schema failures), function-call execution rate, and any fallback invocations. We'll provide a starter benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:20] Jordan: about dedicated / private: we might need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. can you confirm?
[06:26] Maya: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private supports customer KMS/HSM plus on-prem options. There are some network setup steps - we'll include a checklist.
[06:35] Ethan: audit logs: are the raw prompts stored? for compliance we may need redact or retention controls.
[06:41] Priya: you can enable prompt redaction and configure retention windows per-project; audit logs are immutable for a retention period you set for compliance.
[06:48] Alex: what's the pricing model for a pilot? can we get reserved capacity?
[06:52] Maya: for pilots we usually do short-term reserved capacity to get predictable throughput, or usage-based if uncertain. I'll send a pricing sheet with both options.
[07:02] [07:20] Samira: can we see a failure mode - like model returns extra fields - show what Console does.
[07:25] Carlos: (runs altered prompt) model returned: {"order_id": "12346", "risk_score": "high", "recommended_action": "expedite", "notes": "call customer"} - Console highlights "risk_score" type mismatch and "expedite" not in enum. In strict mode this fails build; in permissive mode it emits warnings and strips unrecognized fields.
[07:49] Jordan: is there an SDK-level error code so our ingestion pipeline can track these failures?
[07:55] Carlos: yes SDK returns structured response with status codes: OK, VALIDATION_WARNING, VALIDATION_ERROR, TOOL_BLOCKED. You can instrument metrics accordingly.
[08:06] Alex: nice. about function calling - can the functions call out to our internal microservices or do we have to proxy through Redwood?
[08:14] Carlos: for hosted we offer secure webhook execution (we sign calls), or you can run function execution in your environment with a small connector that receives the parsed call. For Private, execution stays in your network.
[08:29] Ethan: what about RBAC - can we limit which team can define tool runners?
[08:33] Priya: yes, Console has role-based permissions; only admins can register tools and change execution policies.
[08:40] [09:05] Maya: a few real-customer notes: one retailer used schema enforcement to reduce downstream errors by 40% and used mappings to convert vendor-specific codes. Another customer used function-calling to automate refunds and saw mean time to resolution drop.
[09:20] Samira: good to hear. any constraints on size of schema or nested objects?
[09:26] Carlos: deep nesting can add validation cost, but we support typical nested JSON objects up to a practical complexity. For very deep structures we recommend validating at multiple route stages.
[09:36] Alex: ok, last product question - can we run A/B tests on model variants for the same route?
[09:41] Maya: yes, Console supports rollouts, canary, and AB tests by traffic split and also automatic fallback. You can tie eval metrics to rollouts.
[09:50] Jordan: there's often tradeoff between cheaper quantized models and output quality. any guidance?
[09:56] Carlos: Optimize offers model suggestions per workload - we analyze prompt set and suggest quantization profiles and batching to hit cost targets with minimal quality loss. We can run a quick evaluation during pilot.
[10:08] [10:30] Alex: ok, sounds good. for next steps we'll need: pricing, security docs (SOC 2, ISO), and a benchmark plan.
[10:37] Maya: noted. we'll send docs and calendar invite for a pilot kickoff.
[10:42] Samira: who will manage the pilot from Redwood side?
[10:45] Maya: Carlos will be your SE for the pilot. I'm the AE and will coordinate commercial.
[10:51] Carlos: we'll also share a sample schema and a starter prompt set.
[10:55] Ethan: one last question - do you have pre-built evals for hallucination metrics?
[11:00] Priya: yes Console supports custom evals and we have pre-built hallucination checks and entity-extraction accuracy tests.
[11:09] Alex: great. thanks everyone.
[11:12] Maya: thanks all - recap in chat and next steps in email.
[11:16] [11:45] End of recording
